summary.intent: Execute all 7 plans of Phase 21 (BYO IPFS Node Support) via wave-based parallel execution, verify end-to-end functionality through UAT, then create gap closure plans for issues found during testing.
summary.outcome: All 7 plans executed and committed. Six bugs found and fixed during Playwright UAT. Full cipherbox→external Kubo migration verified (44/44 CIDs, ~14s for 100MB). Four gap closure plans (21-08 through 21-11) created for remaining issues. Branch merged with main.

repo: TEE worker is not in the pnpm workspace — requires separate npm install and inline env var injection (no .env auto-loading via tsx watch)
Auth store is memory-only with no localStorage persistence — test-login API creates a duplicate auth_methods row that conflicts with subsequent email OTP login for the same identity
Migration processor used env var TEE_AUTH_SECRET while the rest of the codebase (TeeService) uses TEE_WORKER_SECRET — inconsistency caused silent processor failures
StorageTab encrypted provider configs with bytesToHex but TEE worker's decryptEcies decoded them as base64 — ECIES ciphertext corruption in-enclave
SSRF protection in migration-worker blocks 192.168.* by default, which also blocks local dev Kubo nodes; simulator bypass flag needed
DualPinProvider exists in sdk-core but the web app's upload flow (useDropUpload) does not invoke the secondary pin — dual-write is config-only, not functional
Pinata deprecated their standard PSA endpoint (/psa returns 404); Filebase IPFS RPC uses non-standard auth — only self-hosted Kubo works reliably with current providers
Browser-side connection test is blocked by CORS for all SaaS pinning services; architectural fix is to route through TEE worker (already handles ECIES decrypt → use credentials pattern)
Migration trigger condition requires savedConfig !== null, but first-time users switching from default cipherbox mode have no IPNS record yet — first switch never triggers migration
DHCP can reassign the QEMU bridge host IP; all .env service addresses may need updating after Docker stack recreates

code.finding: Checked TEE_AUTH_SECRET env var instead of TEE_WORKER_SECRET used everywhere else — processor silently failed all migration jobs
decryptEcies used Buffer.from(encryptedBase64, 'base64') but StorageTab sends hex strings via bytesToHex — encoding mismatch caused 'bad point: got length 65' secp256k1 error
parseProviderConfig type only accepted 'psa' | 'kubo' — 'cipherbox' source protocol (default mode users) caused type error and unhandled fetch path

Migration trigger: const providerChanged = savedConfig && ... — null check on savedConfig prevents migration for first-time users switching from default cipherbox mode; fix treats null as implicit cipherbox
HTTP 401/403/422 responses from probed endpoint fell through as 'protocol not detected' instead of 'authentication failed' — both Kubo and PSA probes needed explicit status code handling

workflow: Background task output files at /private/tmp/claude-501/.../tasks/*.output contain API console logs including OTP codes — faster than asking the user
API hot-reload via Nest watch does not guarantee the fix takes effect if port 3000 is still held by a prior process — EADDRINUSE silently prevents the reloaded instance from binding

BullMQ jobs are persisted in Redis and picked up by new processor instances on startup — stale failed jobs from a prior broken processor can be immediately retried by a new instance before the fix is applied
Playwright MCP browser_fill_form with large file uploads (100MB) can crash the page — upload files one at a time or in small batches
GSD checkpoint continuation agents require explicit completed_tasks_table, resume_task_number, and user_response fields — spawning without them produces incomplete SUMMARY commits

friction: Docker host DHCP reassignment changed IP from 192.168.133.114 to 192.168.133.12 — required updating 5 entries in apps/api/.env mid-session
Redis port in .env was 6380 but service was on 6379 — required explicit nc port testing to diagnose
TEE worker not in pnpm workspace required separate npm install; no .env loading meant inline env vars were needed every time the worker was restarted
Multiple API hot-reload failures (EADDRINUSE) made it impossible to test processor fixes without a full kill-and-restart cycle
test-login API call created a duplicate auth_methods row that broke subsequent email OTP login for the same user — required switching to a different email mid-session
Playwright session lost auth state on page crash from large upload, requiring full re-login
Migration UI displayed stale 'failed' state after processor was fixed and new migration completed — component polls /migration/status which returned the old completed (failed) job
Pinata deprecated PSA and Filebase uses non-standard auth — both major SaaS providers non-functional with current implementation; only self-hosted Kubo worked for UAT
CORS blocked all SaaS provider connection tests in the browser — significant testing blocker that revealed the architectural gap late in execution
open_items: 21-08: Wire DualPinProvider into web app upload flow (useDropUpload/sdk-provider) — dual-write config saves but secondary pin is never invoked during upload
21-08: Add source unpin step after successful migration — current implementation is copy-only with no cleanup
21-09: Replace browser-side connection test with TEE-routed endpoint — POST /tee/connection-test with ECIES-wrapped config, TEE decrypts and probes, returns result to UI
21-10: PinataProvider using Pinata's proprietary /v3/files API (PSA endpoint deprecated) — required for SaaS BYO users
21-11: Run BYO performance benchmarks against real external IPFS provider and capture .planning/baselines/21-byo-baselines.md — deferred, needs provider infrastructure
1 CID failed in reverse migration (external→cipherbox) — likely CIDv0/CIDv1 version mismatch between nodes; needs investigation
Migration retrigger UX: after a failed migration is 'completed' in DB, UI has no way to retrigger without switching modes twice — needs explicit retry button or status-aware trigger logic
SSRF bypass is currently hardcoded for simulator mode — production TEE needs an allowlist mechanism for private network endpoints that are legitimately user-owned Kubo nodes
